note: Three interpretations of a hardening rule, ordered by OSCAL layer rather than rank. The analysis uses a working definition without selecting an interpretation. Each view links to a stakeholder glossary term. The advocate and quote fields retain provenance and are not rendered, following the Gate 7 decision.
why_this_matters: Pre-read criterion 3 identifies the absence of an OSCAL requirement-level field. The gap affects every approach; model placement has become a proxy for whether authors treat guidance as requirements, capabilities or assessment procedures.

views.label: A requirement
views.definition: A binding requirement, expressed as a shall. A rule differs from a regulatory control in specificity.

views.label: A capability statement
views.definition: A description of possible component configurations. The technology provider describes capabilities; the adopting organisation sets requirements.
views.advocate: Anca Sailer and Vikas Agarwal, IBM

views.label: An assessor's procedure
views.definition: A procedure for applying or verifying hardening guidance. Assessment activities and steps describe the work, with executable checks referenced for automation.

crux.note: Brian Ruf's objection applies to any option, not only to the one it was raised against.

automation_argument.claim: The automation argument treats applying and verifying hardening guidance as operational work, not just a finer-grained form of regulatory control. Automation coverage varies across the published guides.
automation_argument.claim_not_made: Hardening guidance is never performed manually. The corpus includes manual procedures and does not support that claim.

evidence.manual: 144 steps, covering every step; every activity carries method EXAMINE
evidence.note: This guide provides a counterexample to the claim that all hardening procedures are automated.

working_definition.text: One technical requirement or recommendation, finer-grained than a control, without any claim about whether it is binding.
working_definition.status: A working definition for comparing the three approaches without selecting an interpretation.
